messages:
riley: Idea: a burst-aware precision policy. For short high-throughput bursts we prefer int8 to avoid p95 spikes from 4bit kernels; for steady-state low-novelty streams we can go to 4bit. simple rules, low-risk. Thoughts? cc @hao @maya

hao: makes sense. define burst = arrival_rate > X req/s over sliding 5s? what X?

riley: start with X=30 req/s per-node as conservative. runtime measures rate per routing shard and tags convs as `burst_candidate` for 10s. policy: if burst -> avoid 4bit; else consider 4bit when novelty low and batch_size>=4.

maya: cache compatibility: if we change precision within a conversation, don't reuse existing kv namespace. prefer: only switch when conv has no cached state, or create separate namespace and track cost. also need per-conv precision_history in traces.

hao: telemetry: collect arrival_rate, burst_flag, precision.variant, batch_size, seq_len, deg_shadow, latency.p95. add automatic disable if deg_shadow.mean >0.08 or p95 increases 30% over baseline.

riley: API surface: header `X-Precision-Mode: burst-aware-v1`. optional tunables in body: burst_threshold, burst_window_sec, min_batch_for_4bit. runtime decides per-request. include `precision.sample_id` in trace for correlation.

ops-bot: deploybot: staging canary scheduled with flag `burst_aware_precision=true` at 18:00 UTC. monitor arrival_rate distribution and precision.variant ratio for first 10m.

maya: action items: @hao add telemetry schema and alert thresholds, @riley add runtime pseudo-code and cache appendix, ops-bot wait for QA signoff.

riley: will add a tiny sim harness to replay burst patterns and measure degscore vs fp8 shadow. will post results to the RFC thread. thanks!
